item.title: Bank of Singapore Buys 14% of Bank Capital in $28.04 Mill Year-End Deal
item.description: Jakarta. Ownership at Bank Capital Indonesia (BACA) shifted after Bank of Singapore Limited emerged as a major shareholder in a year-end block transaction, one of the most eye-catching corporate actions in the banking sector this month. According to a share ownership disclosure filed with Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), Bank of Singapore acquired 2.8 billion BACA shares worth Rp 470.40 billion ($28.04 million) on Dec. 19 via a negotiated market deal, at an execution price of Rp 168 per share. item.title: Fatigued Police Get Reinforcements in Sumatra Flood Zones
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia has deployed 1,500 additional police personnel to strengthen disaster response efforts in flood- and landslide-hit areas of Sumatra, as senior officials warn that frontline officers are facing severe physical and psychological fatigue after nearly a month on duty. item.title: Christmas Holiday Brings Tourist Surge Back to Bali
item.description: Bali. Bali is seeing a sharp rise in tourist arrivals during the Christmas and New Year holiday period, signaling a revival in visitor flows after weeks of slower activity linked to bad weather and travel concerns elsewhere in Indonesia. The increase was evident on Friday at the domestic arrivals terminal of I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport, where crowds of travelers from across the country arrived to spend their year-end holidays on the resort island. item.title: Trade Deal: US Seeks Indonesian Critical Minerals for Defense, Auto
item.description: Jakarta. Senior minister Airlangga Hartarto said Friday that the US was eyeing Indonesian critical minerals for automotives and military weapons manufacturing, as they recently settled all substantial issues on an upcoming trade deal. item.title: Malaysia’s Ex-PM Najib Sentenced to 15 Years in Landmark 1MDB Trial
item.description: Putrajaya, Malaysia. Imprisoned former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak was sentenced Friday to 15 years in prison and ordered to pay 13.5 billion ringgit ($3.3 billion) in fines and asset recoveries after being convicted in his largest corruption trial linked to the multibillion-dollar looting of the 1MDB state investment fund. item.title: Indonesian Palm Oil to Get ‘Close to Zero’ Tariffs on Eurasian Trade Pact
item.description: Jakarta. The freshly signed Eurasian trade pact is set to lower the region’s tariffs on Indonesian palm oil “close to zero”, according to a minister. item.title: Nearly 2 Million Travelers Crowd Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta Airport During Year-End Holidays
item.description: Tangerang, Banten. item.title: Thailand, Cambodia Sign New Ceasefire to End Border Fighting
item.description: Bangkok. Thailand and Cambodia on Saturday signed a new ceasefire agreement aimed at ending weeks of armed clashes along their disputed border, a conflict rooted in competing territorial claims. The ceasefire took effect at noon local time. Beyond halting hostilities, the agreement calls on both sides to refrain from further military movements and to avoid violating each other’s airspace for military purposes. item.title: Four Spanish Tourists Missing After Boat Sinks Near Komodo Island
item.description: East Nusa Tenggara. Authorities are continuing search and rescue operations for four Spanish tourists who went missing after a tourist boat sank in waters near Padar Island, part of the Komodo National Park area in Labuan Bajo, East Nusa Tenggara. item.title: Valencia FC Women’s Team Coach, Three Children Missing in Indonesia Boat Accident
item.description: Jakarta. Fernando Martín, a coach with Spanish football club Valencia FC’s women’s team, and three of his children are missing after their boat sank off Labuan Bajo in East Nusa Tenggara on Friday evening. In a social media post, Valencia FC expressed condolences, saying local authorities had confirmed the deaths. Search efforts for the victims continued on Sunday. The vessel was carrying six family members, four crew members, and a local guide when it went down during a trip from Komodo Island
